name: Neo-Nazism
description: Postwar revival of Nazi racial hierarchy and national political authority, with differing economic, organisational and religious variants.

axes.brief: Racial-national authority and rejection of liberal equality favour controlled leadership over universal competitive accountability.
axes.counterEvidence: Some groups stand in elections or organise leaderless cells; tactics do not establish equal pluralism as their proposed national order.

axes.brief: The proposed exclusionary state privileges collective racial control over universal personal liberty.
axes.counterEvidence: Current movements invoke speech and weapons rights against existing governments and differ on medical policy; these claims qualify but do not universalise proposed liberties.

qualifications.12: Neo-Nazi propagandists specifically resist prohibitions on racial incitement; censorship of political enemies is assessed separately.

axes.brief: An ethnically or racially exclusive nation rejects equal multicultural public identity.
axes.counterEvidence: Merely adopting national customs does not necessarily overcome ancestry-based exclusion; different white national traditions can still coexist selectively.

axes.brief: White-national separation and exclusion oppose broad immigration and universal refugee membership.
axes.counterEvidence: Selected co-racial settlers and family migration may be accepted; capacity and skills mechanisms are analogies to selective entry rather than a common published visa code.

axes.brief: Militant racial struggle and national power favour armed coercion beyond strict self-defence.
axes.counterEvidence: Postwar groups vary between revolutionary violence, electoral strategy and territorial separatism; no identical operational foreign policy is assumed.

axes.brief: Racial national sovereignty rejects universal external legal authority while accepting tactical alliances among sympathetic groups.
axes.counterEvidence: Transnational white identity is not necessarily a supranational government or delegation to current institutions.

axes.brief: National-socialist revival suggests conditional private enterprise and strategic collective ownership serving the racial community.
axes.counterEvidence: Economic programmes vary and are less central than racial hierarchy; estimates do not equate all public ownership with neo-Nazism or copy every historical Nazi policy.

axes.brief: Anti-globalism and national productive independence favour strategic trade protection.
axes.counterEvidence: International contacts and selected foreign trade remain possible; tariffs are not uniformly specified across groups.

axes.brief: National productive direction and subordinating finance to collective racial goals qualify ordinary market allocation.
axes.counterEvidence: Many movements lack a detailed economic plan; some retain extensive private enterprise. Coordination answers are contextual rather than universal party-manifesto quotations.

axes.brief: Selective in-group welfare and national solidarity coexist with hierarchy and anti-communism.
axes.counterEvidence: Racial exclusion and differing economic factions make universal egalitarian redistribution a poor fit; targeted provision is not equal rights for all residents.

axes.brief: Political racial authority is generally primary while spiritual or Christian-national recognition varies.
axes.counterEvidence: Christian Identity, Odinist, esoteric and secular currents genuinely conflict; no single religious law is attributed to the entire movement.

qualifications.1: Secular political command and spiritual racial justification compete.
qualifications.2: Religious and secular currents differ substantively on the legal source.

axes.brief: Racial reproduction, patriarchal roles and opposition to homosexuality favour restrictive social conventions.
axes.counterEvidence: Some esoteric and revolutionary factions reject Christian sexual custom; abortion answers are qualified by selective racial reproduction rather than uniform protection of every pregnancy.

axes.brief: Productive national capability and purported racial enhancement favour selected innovation with control of social disruption.
axes.counterEvidence: Nature mysticism and rural revival conflict with technological ambition in some variants; modern medical applications are contextual estimates, not shared published positions.

axes.brief: A unified racial political programme tends to subordinate conflicting local or indigenous institutions.
axes.counterEvidence: Some seek separate enclaves and organise local cells; decentralised tactics are not the same as protected plural constitutional autonomy.

axes.brief: Purported racial heredity and natural sex hierarchy explain core group-difference claims.
axes.counterEvidence: Propaganda and training still aim to change conduct; these answers record ideological beliefs and do not endorse genetic racial superiority or crime explanations.

sources.title: State of white supremacy — neo-Nazi beliefs and distinctions
Blood Tribe — neo-Nazi and Odinist variant

phrase: A society organised around an exclusionary racial nation, with political authority directing institutions toward that nation’s collective goals.

religion.reason: Neo-Nazi currents include Christian Identity, pagan, esoteric and secular variants; the general ideology has no single faith prerequisite.
